question: Nursing informatics combines nursing science with what other two main fields?
explanation: Nursing informatics is an established specialty that integrates nursing, computer, and information sciences to manage patient data effectively. [learn more](GNS113_U1_T7#GNS113_U1_T7_h1)

question: Why is basic computer literacy essential for modern nurses in clinical practice?

options.A: To repair broken circuit boards on ward monitors
options.B: To replace the need for physical bedside nursing care
options.C: To write complex software programs for the hospital
options.D: To manage and communicate patient information accurately

explanation: Nurses use computers daily to handle patient data, document care, and coordinate treatments safely across hospital departments. [learn more](GNS113_U1_T7#GNS113_U1_T7_h1)

question: What is the primary clinical use of a barcode scanner in the ward?

options.B: Printing physical copies of laboratory reports
options.C: Verifying patient identity and scanning medications
options.D: Typing long nursing care plans into the system

explanation: BarcodeInput scanners are critical bedside tools used to match the correct medication to the correct patient wristband. [learn more](GNS113_U1_T7#GNS113_U1_T7_h2)

question: Which item functions strictly as an output device for clinical staff?

options.A: A touchscreen used to select drug dosages
options.B: A barcode scanner reading a patient band
options.C: A computer monitor displaying vital signs
options.D: A computer keyboard used for typing notes

explanation: Monitors present processed data visually to the user without feeding new information back into the system. [learn more](GNS113_U1_T7#GNS113_U1_T7_h2)

question: What happens to data stored in RAM when the computer loses power?

options.A: It remains frozen until power is restored
options.B: It is completely erased because RAM is volatile
options.C: It is automatically saved to the main hard drive
options.D: It is transferred to a secure cloud server

explanation: RAM requires continuous electrical power to maintain its data, making it temporary memory. [learn more](GNS113_U1_T7#GNS113_U1_T7_h3)

question: The Central Processing Unit is primarily responsible for performing which computer function?

options.A: Storing historical patient records for ten years
options.B: Capturing digital images of X-ray scans
options.C: Printing physical documents for hospital administration
options.D: Executing program instructions and processing data

explanation: The CPU performs the core calculations and logical operations that run software applications and process user inputs. [learn more](GNS113_U1_T7#GNS113_U1_T7_h3)

question: What is the main advantage of Solid State Drives over traditional hard drives in a hospital?

options.A: They consume more electricity to boost processing
options.B: They only store temporary data during active tasks
options.C: They have no moving parts and are faster
options.D: They rely on spinning magnetic platters for storage

explanation: SSDs use flash technology, which increases speed and durability compared to mechanical disk drives. [learn more](GNS113_U1_T7#GNS113_U1_T7_h4)

question: Why must hospitals use permanent storage devices instead of relying only on system memory?

options.A: To make the computer boot up faster each morning
options.B: To retain patient records securely over long periods
options.C: To allow the CPU to process vital signs instantly
options.D: To prevent the monitor from dimming during shifts

explanation: Permanent storage ensures that clinical notes, lab results, and legal documents are preserved even when devices are powered down. [learn more](GNS113_U1_T7#GNS113_U1_T7_h4)

question: What is the primary role of an operating system in a hospital computer?

options.A: Scanning patient barcodes at the bedside medication cart
options.B: Storing permanent backup files for discharged patients
options.C: Providing physical protection against accidental liquid spills
options.D: Managing hardware resources and providing a user interface

explanation: The operating system controls system hardware and lets users interact with applications like electronic health records. [learn more](GNS113_U1_T7#GNS113_U1_T7_h5)

question: Which software category do electronic health record programs belong to?
explanation: Clinical programs designed for specific tasks like charting and medication tracking are classified as application software. [learn more](GNS113_U1_T7#GNS113_U1_T7_h5)

question: What type of network connects computers within a single hospital building or ward?
explanation: A Local Area Network links devices within a limited geographic space like a single healthcare facility. [learn more](GNS113_U1_T7#GNS113_U1_T7_h6)

question: A nurse in the emergency unit views lab results just ordered by a doctor in the outpatient clinic. What enables this shared access?

options.A: Connected computer networks running electronic health records
options.B: Independent operating systems stored on local USB drives
options.C: Permanent hard disk storage attached to the patient bed
options.D: High-capacity random access memory inside the bedside monitor

explanation: Networks tie computers together, allowing different hospital units to access centralized patient data in real time. [learn more](GNS113_U1_T7#GNS113_U1_T7_h6)

question: Which practice represents a serious breach of patient data security by a nurse?

options.A: Reporting a broken password prompt to IT support
options.B: Locking the computer screen before leaving the desk
options.C: Logging out of the electronic health record after charting
options.D: Sharing personal login passwords with another colleague

explanation: Sharing passwords compromises accountability and violates patient privacy protocols by allowing unauthorized system access. [learn more](GNS113_U1_T7#GNS113_U1_T7_h7)

question: Why is role-based access control important in electronic health record systems?

options.A: To limit staff viewing only to information relevant to their duties
options.B: To prevent the operating system from crashing during emergencies
options.C: To make computer processing speeds faster for doctors
options.D: To reduce the storage space needed for old patient files

explanation: Role-based access ensures that hospital staff only see the patient files necessary for their specific clinical responsibilities. [learn more](GNS113_U1_T7#GNS113_U1_T7_h7)
